div.head: ECf 16
div.ab: Murdra quidem inuenta fuerunt tempore Cnuti regis; qui post adquisitam terram et secum pacificatam, remisit domum exercitum suum precatu baronum de terra.
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 642 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

note.seg: Cnut sandte Dänische Schiffe heim und verjagte später Herzöge; verwirrt Verf. Beides? Eine Bitte der Witan um Heeres-Entlassung, an sich möglich, erfand er vielleicht wie Ähnliches für Eadward III. und für 1070: 34, 3. 34, 1a. Denn dass Grosse, z. Th. Dänen oder ihnen verwandt, sich Cnut fürs Engländervolk verbürgten, wäre beispiellos

Cnut sent Danish ships home and later drove out earls; does the author confuse the two? A request by the witan for the army to be dismissed, possible in itself, he perhaps invented, like similar things for Edward III and for 1070: 34, 3. 34, 1a. For that magnates, partly Danes or related to them, stood surety to Cnut for the English people would be without precedent

div.ab: Murder-fines (murdra) were indeed devised in the time of King Cnut; who, after the land had been acquired and pacified with himself, sent his army back home at the request of the barons of the land.
